card.summary: None. It was 15 GB for early Galaxy buyers, cut to 5 GB for new accounts, then discontinued. Gallery Sync and Drive migrated to Microsoft OneDrive

free_tier.stated: None. It was 15 GB for early Galaxy buyers, cut to 5 GB for new accounts, then discontinued. Gallery Sync and Drive migrated to Microsoft OneDrive

retention.stated: Two-phase shutdown: Gallery Sync and Drive migrated by 2021-09-30, then the remaining sync. Samsung matched the old quota on OneDrive for one year only, after which OneDrive's 5 GB applies

record.tooling: none usable. Samsung's own support pages redirect the user to their personal OneDrive account
record.chaining: Nothing to chain: it is now literally OneDrive on a 5 GB free tier. The 15 GB that older guides quote is a number that no longer exists

limits.value: the storage product was discontinued and migrated to OneDrive by 2021-09-30

identity_cost.detail: a Samsung account, which now gives OneDrive and not Samsung storage

record.reliability_note: Do not count this as a live 15 GB. The quota Samsung matched on OneDrive lasted one year and OneDrive's own 5 GB applied afterwards

evidence.proved: 'Your Gallery app can only be synced to your personal OneDrive account', so the Samsung-side storage is gone
Samsung's own notice page, 'Sync with OneDrive ending soon'
'dozens of cloud storage companies have either given up on free cloud storage (e.g Samsung, Amazon and Ionos)'

record.binding_note: The storage product ended, so the retention clamp is total and there is no offer to test.
record.notes: Covers consumer Samsung Cloud device gallery storage, distinct from Samsung SDS enterprise cloud. Consumer file drive services and gallery sync were officially decommissioned in 2021 with data migrated to Microsoft OneDrive.

extras.cross_topic_note: a different product from the same company: compute/samsung-cloud.json covers Samsung SDS Cloud Platform
